title: Crime & Noir
tagline: From Ocean's Eleven to Once Upon a Time in America without noticing the water got hot.

levels.note: Charming crooks, cockney chaos and Clooney.

core.b: Clooney, Pitt and a crew of charmers rob three Vegas casinos at once. Cool, funny, and nobody really gets hurt.

br.note: DiCaprio's teenage con man and Tom Hanks's dogged FBI agent

Magician bank robbers. Silly, slick and nonsense

core.t: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels

br.note: Ritchie again: a stolen diamond, bare-knuckle boxing and Brad Pitt's unintelligible traveller
Daniel Craig's cocaine middleman wants out

core.b: Soderbergh: George Clooney's charming bank robber and Jennifer Lopez's marshal fall for each other in a car boot. Elmore Leonard's dialogue.

br.note: Tarantino's Elmore Leonard film: Pam Grier outwits everyone
John Travolta's loan shark goes into the movie business
Terence Stamp's Cockney ex-con hunts his daughter's killer in LA

br.note: The Coens' first: a Texas bar owner hires a killer
Two brothers find a crashed plane full of money

br.note: The heist gone wrong, told from the warehouse
Tarantino's script, Tony Scott's film: lovers on the run with the mob's cocaine

br.note: The Hong Kong original. Core on the Asian action ladder
Mann's Pacino vs De Niro. Core on the Action ladder

br.note: Denzel Washington's corrupt narcotics cop
Al Pacino, the honest cop nobody will back
Denzel's Harlem heroin king vs Russell Crowe's honest cop
Sidney Lumet: a detective informs on his own unit

seq.note: Young Vito and older Michael. Maybe even better

br.note: Johnny Depp undercover with Al Pacino's small-time hood

br.note: De Niro, Pesci and Sharon Stone run Vegas into the ground

Scorsese's three-and-a-half-hour gangster farewell
DiCaprio's stockbroker crook: three hours of excess

br.note: Michael Caine's cold Newcastle revenge. On the Action ladder
Ray Winstone's retired safecracker vs Ben Kingsley's terrifying recruiter
Cronenberg: Viggo Mortensen's Russian mob driver, and the bathhouse fight

br.note: The Naples Camorra, without glamour

Dick Powell's Marlowe
Bogart's violent screenwriter suspected of murder

Carol Reed: James Mason's wounded IRA man adrift in Belfast

Rita Hayworth, 'Put the Blame on Mame'

Cagney and Bogart in Prohibition New York

br.note: John Huston's jewel heist and the crew that ruins it
Early Kubrick: a racetrack heist told out of order

core.b: Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway rob banks across Depression Texas, and the ending changed screen violence.

br.note: Terrence Malick: Martin Sheen and Sissy Spacek's killing spree as a dreamy romance

br.warn: Extreme drug use and sexual content.

core.t: Once Upon a Time in America
